Quagmire

KWAG-mire -- from 'quag' (a bog) plus 'mire' (a swamp). · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Quagmire is a difficult, complicated situation that is hard to escape.

The merger negotiations turned into a legal quagmire, with lawyers on both sides trading objections for over a year.

Worked Example

What started as a simple request to fix a billing error somehow required four different departments, a dozen phone transfers, and three months of unreturned emails.

A tangled, drawn-out mess like that -- one that's genuinely hard to get out of -- is exactly what a quagmire is.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

morass: A morass is a confusing tangle of many interlocking details -- a morass of rules, forms, and exceptions -- and the word stresses the sheer disorienting mass of it. A quagmire stresses being trapped: the harder you struggle to get out, the deeper you sink.

dilemma: A dilemma is a forced choice between exactly two options, each carrying a serious downside. A quagmire involves no choosing at all -- it is a tangled situation that has already trapped you, where every attempt to move leads deeper in.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

solution: a way of solving a problem or difficulty

simplicity: the quality of being easy and uncomplicated

Where it sits · how hard the mess is to escape — predicament → quagmire → quicksand

predicament vs. quagmire: A predicament is any difficult situation, even a small, short-lived one, like realizing you left your keys inside a locked house. A quagmire is a stronger word reserved for messes that drag on and on, resisting every attempt to escape.

quicksand vs. quagmire: Figurative quicksand is harsher than a quagmire: a quagmire drags at you and slows every escape, but quicksand swallows people outright -- getting free by yourself is impossible, not just difficult.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — quag-

root — quag-: a bog, marshy ground (dialectal, related to 'quake') (Middle English)

root — -mire

root — -mire: a swampy or muddy area (Old Norse (myrr))

Put it together

Put it together: Quagmire literally combines quag ('a bog') and mire ('a swamp') -- so a quagmire is, quite literally, ground you sink into, which is exactly what a hopeless, tangled situation feels like.

Use the root in a new word: mire

Use the root in a new word: mire: The truck's back wheels sank deeper into the mire with every attempt to reverse.
